title: Correcting the Ellington myths: Ring Them Bells chimes and the maracas date
summary: Barnet denies ever playing chimes on Ellington's Ring Them Bells, but says he played maracas on a 1937 Barney Bigard small-band date at Irving Mills's request for a Latin sound.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Okay. You said that one of the first things you wanted to do on here was correct a many times repeated legend, right, about --
Well, yes. It's one of those things that keeps cropping up in discographies and some of the people that write the books, about the big band era, and it just
never happened. This is the supposed performance of me on the chimes on Duke Ellington's record of "Ring Them Bells." It just never happened and I have no idea how it ever got started.
But while we were talking about that, while we were setting up the tape recorder, you did mention something that you did on an Ellington record, which was what?

Well, I was pressed into service, more or less in an emergency, because they wanted more Latin sounds, I was pressed into service as a maraca player on one of the small band, Ellington band dates, under Barney Bigard's name, which I believe was -- I think the tune was "Moonlight Fiesta".

And we looked that up in Benny Aslin's (PHONETIC) discography, and we found out that that date was June 16th, 1937, and it was a date with Barney Bigard, Harry Carney, Rex Stewart, Juan Tizol, Duke Ellington, Freddie Guy, Billy Taylor and Sonny Greer.
And it credits you with maracas. Where was that recording, the session?
That was done in New York at the Master Records, Variety Record Studios, the Irving Mills Recording Company.
I see. And you said it was Irving Mills didn't feel they could spare a horn player to play

Well, he wanted more of a Latin sound than they were getting there, and of course Sonny was the only percussionist there at the moment, and so he suggested that I play the maracas, and that's how I happened to -- I happened to be in the studio.
